events.label: FOMC Minutes — July 28–29 meeting; three hawkish dissenters
events.note: Updated Aug 18 morning: A vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz Tuesday morning (one casualty), shifting the Hormuz risk premium from negotiation-failure to physical supply disruption — an escalation that makes a hawkish dissent read more durable even if September hike odds remain near 30%. Three hawkish dissenters from the July 28-29 hold vote (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan); 9 of 18 FOMC participants penciling in a 2026 hike. Critical question: was the dissent driven by fiscal sustainability and Treasury supply-absorption concerns, or by CPI persistence? Fiscal sustainability is not tempered by soft demand data. September hike odds ~30%, down from 82% late-July peak. A dovish (CPI-only) read compresses 30Y toward 5.20–5.25%; a fiscal-sustainability read extends toward 5.40%.

events.label: Target (TGT) Q2 2026 earnings — general merchandise and consumer confidence read
events.note: Added Aug 17 night. TGT's general merchandise data reads directly through UMich's 51.0 consumer sentiment (lowest since February). Combined with HD same day, two guidance misses on comparable-store sales confirms structural consumer deceleration rather than June pull-forward. One miss is noise; two is a pattern.

events.label: Walmart (WMT) Q2 2026 earnings — highest-signal consumer read of the week
events.note: Added Aug 17 night. WMT's traffic commentary spans grocery, general merchandise, and pharmacy across income cohorts — the most comprehensive consumer-spending signal of the retail gauntlet. Look for per-visit spend trends and whether the consumer mix is shifting toward lower-margin grocery and away from discretionary general merchandise. In-line or above-consensus comparable-store guidance would challenge the structural deceleration narrative; a miss alongside HD/TGT confirms it.

events.label: SPCX next staggered tranche (~7%) — second unlock after Aug 6 first tranche
events.note: Updated Aug 17 night: 30Y breached 5.28% to close at 5.31% (19-year high) and Brent crossed $90 on Hormuz escalation — both are headwinds for the rate-compression thesis underlying the SPCX long case. SPCX absorbed the first tranche at $105–$115 (Aug 6–7); current ~$140. WMT earnings same day — consumer data provides macro context for the lock-up absorption. October Q3 Starlink profitability remains the fundamental anchor. Front-run signal: close below $120 on elevated volume before Aug 20.

events.label: NVDA Q2 FY27 earnings (est.) — chip sector at 5.5% selloff, DDR5 legal risk adds supply-chain variable
events.note: Updated Aug 18 night: SOXX fell 5.5% and MU fell 7.6% on Netlist's new ITC + federal patent actions targeting DDR5 server memory products — DDR5 sits at the base of the HBM supply chain underpinning AI workloads. AMD fell 5%, NVDA fell 2.19%. Netlist ITC proceedings run 12–18 months; market prices headline before merits. The altitude ceiling (CSCO, AMAT, AVGO, MSFT/META hyperscaler read-through) gains a fifth signal: supply-chain legal friction at the DDR5/HBM layer. Bar unchanged: gross margin above 78% AND data-center guide materially above the most aggressive sell-side estimate — both simultaneously required. 30Y at 5.31% adds rate compression. Jackson Hole begins Aug 27 — no de-risk window between the print and Warsh's keynote.

events.label: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium (Aug 27–29) — Warsh keynote; 30Y at 19-year high
events.note: Updated Aug 17 night: 30Y closed at 5.31% (19-year high, first breach of 5.28% trigger) and Brent crossed $90 on Hormuz escalation entering Jackson Hole. Five consecutive soft data prints (NFP −23K, CPI core 2.5%, PPI flat, retail sales −0.6% MoM, UMich prelim 51.0) argue for patience; Hormuz oil-shock premium and fiscal sustainability concerns argue for hawkishness. FOMC Minutes (Aug 19) preview which framing the committee leans on. NVDA earnings land Aug 26 — one day before the keynote. UMich final (due Aug 28, during Jackson Hole) is a within-symposium data point. Dovish Warsh message compresses 30Y toward 5.10% and September odds below 20%. Hawkish message (SPR at 40-year lows, Hormuz disruption, UMich inflation expectations elevated) re-anchors 30Y above 5.35%.

events.label: AVGO Q3 FY2026 earnings (est.) — VMware liability and AI concentration: first post-exploitation read
events.note: Added Aug 14 night: AVGO fell 4.1% to $389.79 on August 14 on two simultaneous headwinds: VMware CVE-2026-59310 active exploitation (361 IPs, 47 countries) and guidance implying AI accounts for ~72% of next-quarter sequential revenue growth. Q3 FY2026 results (est. early September, approximately September 4-5 based on Q2 reporting June 3) are the first public accounting of both: whether VMware remediation costs appear in the financial guidance, whether enterprise customers cited the incident, and whether AI revenue breadth (or concentration) shifts the multiple conversation. At ~65x trailing P/E, any miss or margin compression compounds. The $380 structural support level and $400 resistance are the two levels to monitor heading into the print.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.
